sources.entry: Mailpit | Email and SMTP testing tool with a web UI for developers

summary.one_liner: Mailpit is a small, fast, zero-dependency email testing tool that acts as an SMTP server with a web UI and REST API for capturing and inspecting developer test emails.
summary.what_it_does: Mailpit runs as a single static binary or multi-architecture Docker image and acts as an SMTP server that captures outgoing mail. Its web UI lets you search and view messages as formatted HTML, highlighted HTML source, text, headers, raw source, and MIME attachments (with image thumbnails), with optional HTTPS and authentication. A REST API supports automated integration testing. Additional features include an optional POP3 server, HTML compatibility checks, link and linked-image checks, spam scoring via a running SpamAssassin server, screenshots of HTML messages, message tagging, SMTP relaying and forwarding, a chaos mode for injecting SMTP errors, and an optional webhook for received messages. Real-time updates use web sockets, and old mail is pruned by volume or age (default keeps the most recent 500).
use_cases: test email sending in automated integration tests
inspect HTML email rendering and client compatibility
replace MailHog for local SMTP testing
test application resilience to SMTP errors
check links and spam score in test emails
forward or relay captured mail to a real SMTP server
how_to_run: Install via script: sudo sh (Linux & Mac, installs to /usr/local/bin/mailpit; script URL truncated in README)
Run the mailpit binary; web UI on port 8025 and SMTP on 0.0.0.0:1025 by default
notable: Single static binary with no dependencies
Built-in chaos mode for simulating SMTP failures
Inspired by and positioned as a successor to MailHog
Optional SMTP relaying with recipient allowlist and automatic forwarding
Mobile and tablet HTML preview toggle
caveats: README is truncated in places, so some install details (script URL, default web port) are incomplete in the source given
Spam checking requires a separately running SpamAssassin server
A hosted team-features product (Mailtrap) is promoted in the README as a companion, not part of Mailpit itself
